title: Circumference Formula via Differentiation of Area
description: Derives the circumference formula C(r) = 2πr by differentiating the area formula A(r) = πr². Formalizes the deep connection: C(r) = dA/dr. Extends Wiedijk #9 (Area of a Circle) with the circumference derivation. 15 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The formula C(r) = 2πr is usually taken as a definition or proved geometrically. The differentiation approach (C = dA/dr) provides a deeper analytic understanding: the circumference is the rate of change of area, reflecting that a thin annular strip has area ≈ C(r)·dr.
overview.problemStatement: Prove C(r) = 2πr by formally differentiating A(r) = πr² using Mathlib's calculus library.
overview.proofStrategy: Define A(r) = π·r² as a real function. Prove it has derivative 2πr using HasDerivAt. Connect to measure-theoretic area via ENNReal.toReal. State circumference as the derivative.
keyInsights: **Geometric interpretation**: when a disk grows by dr, the added area is a thin annular strip of width dr and circumference C(r): dA ≈ C(r)·dr. Differentiating gives C(r) = dA/dr.
**Higher-dimensional generalization**: surface area of n-ball = derivative of n-ball volume w.r.t. radius — the same pattern holds in all dimensions.
**Wiedijk #9 extension**: the formal area A(r) = πr² is Wiedijk's result; this adds the differentiation step to get circumference.

conclusion.implications: The differentiation derivation of circumference is arguably the most elegant proof and generalizes to higher dimensions (surface area = derivative of volume).
openQuestions: Can the n-ball surface area = derivative of volume be proved in Lean?
Can the isoperimetric inequality (C² ≥ 4πA) be derived from this framework?
